text:
evan: FYI customer 'Acadia' reports SSE stream stops mid-payload when requests traverse an intermediate API gateway. They see a partial event, then connection drops. When client reconnects it gets the remainder as a new stream and is billed for both. Repro steps below.

mira: Can you paste the minimal repro and any gateway config?

evan: Repro (from customer):
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.acadia.example/v1/stream"
They run through an envoy-based gateway that does h2->h1 translation to our edge. Gateway timeout is 30s, keepalive 15s.

jamie: Any server logs or connect traces?

evan: Server logs show: "client closed connection: upstream reset by peer" followed by stream flush partial chunk. No explicit error from runtime. Attached gateway logs show "upstream response ended with zero-length chunk" from the h1 proxy.

nishant: This sounds like chunked transfer semantics being mishandled when converting h2 DATA frames to h1 chunked encoding. Some intermediaries drop the final chunk or send premature FIN.

mira: Are they using grpc-gateway or straight proxy? many customers accidentally plumb gRPC web in front of SSE and it mangles streaming semantics.

evan: They confirmed an in-house gateway that also exposes gRPC endpoints. The path uses a translation layer for some routes.

sre-bot: incident:auto-detect - potential pattern matched: "h2->h1 intermediate chunk-boundary". Count: 4 occurrences in last 24h for same customer.

jamie: Quick mitigation: recommend setting the gateway to passthrough HTTP/2 for SSE routes or enable "preserve-frames" mode if available. Also increase keepalive to >60s so the gateway doesn't prematurely close idle connections during long streams.

mira: Can we confirm billing side: are we counting tokens when partial stream delivered and again when resumed?

evan: Yes customer attached usage snapshots. We currently bill per token produced; resumed stream produces new tokens, partial tokens were already emitted and counted. They expect resume to continue the same session.

nishant: Edge suggestion: add idempotent-resume metadata so resumed streams are attributed to original session (would need client support + ticket). Short term: provide guidance to gateway operators.

jamie: Logging improvement: add a tag on stream end indicating whether final chunk/trailer was observed. If missing, set "stream_truncated":true in traces. That will make root cause detection easier.

mira: Evan, can you collect: gateway config snippet, tcpdump of the h2->h1 conversion, and the runtime trace for the session id? Then we'll escalate to runtime team for a kernel-level check.

evan: Will collect and upload to the thread. Also asked customer to try direct h2 passthrough to our edge as a quick repro.

jamie: For support reply: Ask customer to (1) try bypassing translation for the route, (2) set gateway keepalive >60s, (3) share gateway config and tcpdump. Offer a temporary credit for duplicate billing while we verify.

mira: +1 on the credit. Flagging this for priority support and runtime triage. @jamie @nishant please follow up once we have traces. :eyes:

evan: Uploaded gateway config and a short pcap (S3 link) — I added notes where the stream cuts and the gateway sends an unexpected zero-length chunk.

sre-bot: alert: billing_team notified automatically via #billing for possible double-charge.

jamie: I'll instrument the runtime to log kernel-level writev behavior and chunk boundaries for the next 24h window for this customer.

mira: Thanks team. Evan please post customer-facing response draft in this thread so we can align messaging.

evan: Draft to customer: "Thanks — we're investigating. Quick actions: try h2 passthrough or increase gateway keepalive; we've opened a ticket for runtime analysis and will apply a temporary credit if we confirm double-counting. ETA 48h."

mira: Looks good. Marking this thread for follow-up.
